segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Complement and Anticomplement are the two universal homothety operators centered at the Centroid X two. Because the centroid divides every median in a two-to-one ratio, dilation through X two by negative one-half maps triangle A B C onto its medial triangle.

segments.text: For any center P, its complement lies on line P X two on the opposite side of X two at half the distance, with barycentric coordinates v plus w, w plus u, u plus v. Its anticomplement lies at twice the distance in the opposite direction, with barycentrics negative u plus v plus w, u minus v plus w, u plus v minus w.

segments.text: This single homothety organizes two of the most famous lines in Collection One: on the Euler line, X five is the complement of X three and X four is the anticomplement of X three; on the Nagel line, Spieker center X ten is the complement of Incenter X one and Nagel point X eight is its anticomplement.
